everyAgentLaunchCarriesTheAsyncMarker: CONFIRMED and strong. Measured over 4 real transcripts spanning claude 2.1.278-2.1.283:
177 Agent launches, 177 tool_results with toolUseResult.isAsync true. No exceptions.
everyAgentLaunchIsEventuallyClosedByANot: CORRECTED 2026-09-27. This entry previously said FALSE, citing 19 of 177 launches (10.7%)
never closing plus 11 orphan notifications. **That was a measurement error, not a finding.**
The scan behind it read only ONE of the three sites a notification occupies and matched only
on <tool-use-id>. Re-measured over 40 transcripts / 739 launches: the original method leaves
13 unclosed (1.8%); reading every site and allowing <task-id> == toolUseResult.agentId leaves
4 (0.5%), and those are in flight in files still being written. The 'orphans' were largely
ORDERING: claude can write the queue-operation enqueue BEFORE the launch record it closes, so
file order is not timestamp order. Found by a peer session that re-measured and pushed back.
Still not pinned as a row, but now for an honest reason: it is a whole-session liveness
property ('closed unless the session ended while in flight') that a four-record fixture
cannot carry. It wants a corpus-wide replay row.
aNotificationOccupiesMoreThanOneSite: CONFIRMED and load-bearing. 98 of the notifications in a 40-transcript sweep were found at
the attachment/queued_command site alone. A reader that knows only the user-string site
under-counts completions -- Flight Deck leaked 8 in one file that way, and my own first
measurement of the unclosed rate was wrong for exactly the same reason.

notCaptured: A SYNCHRONOUS Agent launch -- a tool_result for an Agent call WITHOUT isAsync. Every one of
the 177 launches measured was async, so the synchronous arm of the proposed invariant could
not be captured and is not asserted by any row.
absent. Both are known to occur (see verdicts) but are a LIVENESS property over a whole
session, not a shape a three-record fixture can carry.

A launch closed ONLY by <task-id> (agentId) and not by its own tool-use-id -- known to occur (an agent continued via a follow-up message reports under the continuing call's id) but not present in these four records, so no row asserts that fallback yet.
